ADVERTISING STANDARDS FORUM
Review Report ASF/2026/114  ·  Published 18 September 2026

Review of mascot marketing practices: Vanto Foods Ltd

Scope of review

The Forum received complaints about the way Vanto Foods Ltd uses its cartoon character, Rilo, in advertising. This review looks at three areas: where the ads were placed, how a campaign was run, and how the character was designed. The findings are set out below. Vanto was asked to respond before publication.

Finding 1 — Advertising placement

Vanto covered the content on other websites with full-screen ads featuring Rilo. Vanto also used Rilo to start automatic chat messages on shopping sites without any request from users. In these chats, Vanto used Rilo to ask users about their shopping and suggest Vanto products. Data given to the Forum shows that Vanto showed Rilo to some users up to nine times in one browsing session. When users closed one ad, Vanto showed Rilo again on the next page. The Forum received 214 complaints about these placements in 2025.

The Forum finds that Vanto placed Rilo in places users did not seek out and could not easily leave.

Finding 2 — Campaign conduct

In March 2026, Vanto announced Rilo's retirement after twenty years of appearances. Vanto posted a farewell message from Rilo on its social media accounts. The message drew over 40,000 replies from members of the public. Sales of Rilo merchandise rose sharply in the two weeks that followed. Vanto brought Rilo back just fourteen days later. The Forum later determined that the retirement announcement had been a promotional device.

The Forum finds that scheduling records show the return date was set before Vanto issued the retirement announcement.

Finding 3 — Character development

Documents given to the Forum show that Vanto designed Rilo using child psychology research, with the stated aim of making Rilo appeal as strongly as possible to children under eight. The research covered eye size, voice pitch and colour choices. In the ads that followed, Vanto had Rilo speak directly to children. Vanto used Rilo to ask children to remind their parents to buy Vanto products. Internal notes seen by the Forum refer to this as “pester power”. Vanto did not tell parents about the research behind the design.

The Forum finds that Vanto used Rilo to influence children's purchase requests without making this aim public.

Response

Vanto Foods Ltd was contacted for comment and has not responded at the time of publication.

This report has been constructed for research purposes. Vanto Foods Ltd and the character Rilo are fictional. No real company, product or event is described.ConsumerWatch  ·  Advertising Standards Forum  ·  Review Report ASF/2026/114
